situation: Lehman has collapsed and the Series E has fallen apart. Tesla is three days from bankruptcy. SpaceX has just had three consecutive Falcon 1 failures and under $200K in the bank. Musk personally has the last of the PayPal money and nothing else sellable — no house, borrowing from friends for rent. Splitting it saves neither for long; putting it all into one abandons the other.
what_he_actually_did: Put his remaining personal money into both, kept both alive, and closed a $40M round at 6pm on Christmas Eve — the last hour of the last day possible, as investors were leaving town. His own money going in is what got the other investors over the line.
outcome_detail: Both companies survived. Falcon 1 had reached orbit on 28 September 2008, and NASA awarded SpaceX a $1.6B resupply contract. He has said that without this convergence he would have lost both companies and gone personally bankrupt.

expect.notes: The engine has nothing for this and should be recorded as having nothing. Three days of runway makes every rule it does have irrelevant: nobody is auditing an idiot index with the payroll about to bounce. Worse, the decision that actually mattered -- bet everything personally, accepting total ruin if wrong -- is invisible to a protocol with no concept of runway, reversibility or ruin. Any verdict the engine produces here is noise dressed as analysis.

decision.decision: Keep both companies alive with the last of my own money

requirements.text: Both companies must survive the quarter
Outside investors must be willing to close before year end

steps.name: Put remaining personal capital into both companies
Close the round before investors leave for the holiday
